why: D235: landing shows an atoll's present-day name (e.g. 'Haa Dhaalu'). OSM's admin_level=4 relations carry the traditional names in name:en ('South Thiladhunmathi'), so today's names come from this hand table (PLAN Spec issues 12). Each row is keyed by the OSM relation id and pins the name:en it was written against: build-chart refuses to run if the relation's name:en has changed, so a re-used or re-drawn relation cannot silently take another atoll's name. The id written into the chart is the code letters' slug, stable if OSM renumbers a relation. Two relations may share one id: Malé (r6599336), the capital's own administrative unit, is charted as Kaafu, the atoll its islands lie in, because its present-day name 'Malé' is also an island's name, and v1 shows no island's name (AC138, D221). Pending the owner's answer (CH1 report).
source: The administrative atolls and their code names under the Decentralization Act 2010 (Act 7/2010) as listed by the Maldives Bureau of Statistics census tables (Census 2022) and Wikipedia 'Administrative divisions of the Maldives'. Written from those references by the feature-builder on 2026-10-14 without fetching them: to be checked by the owner, who reads the names on landing (D235, DP3).
